speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are experiencing progressive swelling and pain in your right ring finger; tell me, how long has this been going on?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: That sounds like a significant injury; did you hear a "pop" or "snap" at the moment your finger got caught? Also, is there any visible deformity or bruising on the finger right now?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Mallet Finger (Avulsion Fracture of the Extensor Tendon at the DIP Joint).

Based on your history of the finger being forced into flexion by a jersey and your current inability to actively extend the distal interphalangeal joint, this is a classic presentation of a mallet finger. I am requesting images to confirm the extent of the injury. REQUEST IMAGES: X-Ray_Right_Hand

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
